scope: Lifecycle transition correctness and state invariants across queued/provisioning/booting/ready/running/waiting/completed/failed/cancelled/paused/recovery_required/destroyed; state-machine adversarial traces. Files: src/coordinator.ts, src/store.ts, src/domain.ts, src/mcp.ts, src/config.ts, src/providers/*, src/cli/overview.ts action gating, tests/lifecycle.test.ts, tests/helpers.ts, docs/MCP-API.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

findings.title: A permanently failing pause/resume leaves a durable intent that blocks every other control operation, disables the deadline and suppresses reconciliation
findings.evidence: runControl refuses any differing intent while one is pending (src/coordinator.ts:828-829) and that check precedes the redundant-pause early return (:832), so pause/cancel/destroy all throw 'Another worker control operation is pending'. applyControl pause/resume call the provider with no absence handling (:848 pauseWorker, :859 resumeWorker) unlike cancel (:882-889 vmMissing) and destroy (:913 getWorker). step's catch (:510-517) only patches error, so the intent stays durable. step handles the intent before the deadline check (:440-443 vs :452-455). recover returns early for intent-bearing workers (:407), so the confirmed-absence path (:408-419) never records vm_missing or frees capacity. queueMessage refuses messages only for cancel/destroy intents (:201-208). Reproduced with local fakes (/tmp/probes/probe4.test.ts): variant 1 (pause permanently failing, guest alive) -> 'state: running intent: pause ... expired deadline ignored: true', cancel and destroy both throw, guest still running; variant 2 (paused, guest deleted out of band, resume) -> 'after ticks: paused intent: resume vm_missing: false', message acknowledged 'delivery: queued' with dispatches 'sent,pending', force destroy throws.
findings.recommendation: In applyControl pause/resume, catch the provider error and probe the existing vmMissing(w.vm_id); on confirmed absence settle immediately (pause -> previous_state, resume -> previous_state ?? 'ready') with vm_missing true and intent cleared. In runControl let cancel/destroy supersede a pending pause/resume intent. Do not let the w.intent early return in recover skip the absence check for pause/resume intents.

findings.title: pause_worker escapes terminal states and lets reconciliation overwrite the reason a worker settled
findings.evidence: The MCP pause tool (src/mcp.ts:127-140) applies no state gate, and runControl (:816-836) only rejects destroyed/vm_missing/differing intent/non-paused resume/redundant pause, so applyControl pause transitions completed, failed, cancelled and recovery_required workers to the non-terminal 'paused' with previous_state set to the terminal state (:851-855). recover skips only terminal.has(w.state) (:420), so a VM reporting 'stopped' moves the record to recovery_required with error 'VM stopped; inspect before resuming' (:429-432); resume_worker is then refused ('Worker is not paused'). Reproduced (/tmp/probes/probe1.test.ts, probe3.test.ts): 'completed after pause: paused previous_state: completed'; 'failed error: test suite red: 3 failures' -> 'after reconcile: recovery_required error: VM stopped; inspect before resuming previous_state: failed' -> resume THREW 'Worker is not paused'; the original summary survives only in store.result. src/cli/overview.ts:277-283 gates pause to ready/running/waiting, showing the transition is unintended; no lifecycle test pauses a settled worker.
findings.reproduction: cd /tmp/probes && /tmp/bun142/bin/bun test probe1.test.ts (Bun 1.4.2, exit 0, 2 pass); probe3.test.ts reproduces the error clobber before erroring on my own later resume call
findings.recommendation: Reject pause when terminal.has(w.state), keeping cancel/destroy; or keep the terminal state authoritative by having recover() also skip records whose previous_state is terminal and never overwrite error for an already-settled worker.

findings.title: cancel settles as cancelled when quiescence could not be proven, unlike fail and destroy
findings.evidence: quiesce returns 'paused' both for a genuinely paused guest and for the ambiguous case where the OpenCode stop failed, pauseWorker failed and the guest still exists (:739-744). fail maps that to recovery_required (:785-798) and destroy to recovery_required (:918-926), but the cancel path only inspects for 'missing' (:890) and otherwise transitions to cancelled with no error. Code-evidenced; not separately reproduced.
findings.reproduction: Reuse the fake setup of tests/lifecycle.test.ts:505 (exec 'systemctl stop' returning code 1 plus pauseWorker throwing) with intent=cancel instead of an expired deadline.
findings.recommendation: Treat quiesce() === 'paused' as recovery_required in the cancel path, as fail() already does, so an unproven stop is visible and the retained guest is not silently reported as cancelled.
